article_title: Novel Hybrid Peptide Cecropin A (1-8)-LL37 (17-30) with Potential Antibacterial Activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C, L, and C-L treatments at 1x MIC produced visible bacterial surface damage/cellular debris in E. coli CVCC 245 and S. aureus ATCC 25923 by scanning electron microscopy, supporting membrane/surface integrity disruption as an antibacterial mechanism context.
direct_assay_types: scanning electron microscopy of peptide-treated bacterial cells
source_locators: paper.xml::sec=8:2.4 Disruption of Bacterial Cell Surface Structure Integrity
paper.xml::sec=17:4.6 SEM Analysis of Bacterial Cells
source_locator: paper.xml::sec=8:2.4 Disruption of Bacterial Cell Surface Structure Integrity
paper.xml::sec=17:4.6 SEM Analysis of Bacterial Cells
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The source reports SEM-visible debris, surface damage, collapse, or disfiguration after peptide treatment for 1-4 h; Methods 4.6 reports cells treated at 1x MIC before SEM preparation.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct morphology evidence supports cell surface/membrane damage but does not identify a pore architecture, receptor, enzyme, or intracellular target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure captions report S. aureus ATCC 25293 in one place while text and Table 4 use ATCC 25923; preserve this as a figure-caption caution.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C-L reduced viable S. aureus ATCC 25923 and E. coli CVCC 245 concentrations more strongly than parental C or L during the first three hours of the time-kill assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: hybrid peptide C-L against two indicator strains
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Table 4 provides viable-concentration rows across 1-5 h; Methods 4.5 reports 1x MIC treatment and colony counting.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Phenotypic killing-speed evidence; not a direct molecular mechanism by itself.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No exact molecular target is shown by this assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports C-L as a designed hybrid with higher net charge and predicted helical residue percentage than the parent fragments, which is structure-activity context rather than direct mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: hybrid peptide design and computational structure context
source_locators: paper.xml::sec=5:2.1 Primary Structural Parameters of Peptides
source_locator: paper.xml::sec=5:2.1 Primary Structural Parameters of Peptides
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Table 2 reports C-L net charge +8 and predicted helical residue 90.9%; Figure 1 shows predicted secondary structure.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Supports design rationale and possible membrane interaction propensity, but this is not direct biological mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Prediction/software output must not be promoted to direct mechanism.

mechanism_summary: C-L has direct SEM-backed bacterial surface disruption context plus time-kill phenotype and design/structure context; no receptor/enzyme/intracellular target is claimed.

entity_mechanism_summary.C-L: Hybrid peptide with Table 3 MIC/HC50 activity, Table 4 time-kill efficacy, SEM surface-disruption evidence, and Table 2 predicted helical/charge design context.
entity_mechanism_summary.C and L: Parent comparators with Table 3 activity/toxicity, Table 4 time-kill rows, and SEM comparator images; not final lead entities over C-L.

absence_and_boundary_notes: No supplementary assets were present locally; no supplement-derived mechanism value was fabricated.
SEM evidence is direct cell-surface disruption context but not a molecular pore/receptor target assignment.
Predicted helical structure and net charge are design context, not direct mechanism.
